# T5 questions and answers (generated by extra/build_site_inputs.py from Khaled Adawi's ACME RAG corpora; verbatim)

## Answerable

1. Q: Are the NASA PSI raw videos included?
   A: No. Only a curated text knowledge base, source references and import scripts are included; original archives must be downloaded and indexed separately. (RAG chunk QA-017, ACME)
2. Q: How many ACME investigations are there?
   A: Different NASA pages describe five or six depending on inclusion of CFI-G. This package covers four specified PSI accessions. (RAG chunk QA-019, ACME)
3. Q: What is PSI-10 about?
   A: PSI-10 is Flame Design, focused on soot inception/control and robust oxygen-enriched spherical diffusion flames. (RAG chunk QA-001, PSI-10)
4. Q: What are normal versus inverse flames?
   A: Normal and inverse flames reverse the roles of fuel and oxidizer relative to the burner. The configuration must accompany any comparison. (RAG chunk QA-002, PSI-10)
5. Q: Does increasing flow change Flame Design flame size?
   A: The NASA presentation qualitatively reports larger flame sizes with increased reactant flow for the studied conditions; no general numeric relationship is provided here. (RAG chunk QA-003, PSI-10)
6. Q: Can low-soot flames still extinguish?
   A: Yes. Inert dilution or reduced pressure can suppress soot while weakening the flame; extinction must be assessed separately. (RAG chunk QA-004, PSI-10)
7. Q: What is the goal of BRE?
   A: BRE investigates gas-flame emulation of solid/liquid burning and flame persistence/extinction to improve understanding of spacecraft material flammability. (RAG chunk QA-005, PSI-20)
8. Q: Is the BRE burner a real solid material?
   A: No. A porous gas burner emulates selected aspects of condensed-phase burning; it does not directly test every material. (RAG chunk QA-006, PSI-20)
9. Q: Is 25 percent oxygen always safe in microgravity?
   A: No. A NASA BRE summary reports extinction below roughly 25% for studied cases, not a universal safety threshold. (RAG chunk QA-007, PSI-20)
10. Q: How long do BRE flames last?
   A: Some low-momentum BRE flames lasted minutes, but durations vary with oxygen, fuel, size and other conditions. Exact run-level durations require raw data. (RAG chunk QA-008, PSI-20)
11. Q: Can I use this file for material certification?
   A: No. This is a scientific research retrieval corpus; material qualification needs appropriate standards, tests and expert review. (RAG chunk QA-018, PSI-20)
12. Q: How many BRE table rows are there?
   A: This package has no independently validated primary BRE CSV. Secondary reports use 18 or 43 with differing representation; retrieve the specific NASA file version before using a count. (RAG chunk QA-020, PSI-20)
13. Q: What does PSI-22 measure?
   A: E-FIELD Flames explores ion current, electrical forcing and the resulting flame geometry, soot and stability behavior. (RAG chunk QA-009, PSI-22)
14. Q: How much voltage can E-FIELD use?
   A: NASA describes potential differences up to 10 kV between burner and mesh electrode; field strength is a separate variable. (RAG chunk QA-010, PSI-22)
15. Q: What is ion wind?
   A: It is electrically induced bulk gas motion mediated by flame ions that transfer momentum to neutral gas. (RAG chunk QA-011, PSI-22)
16. Q: Is maximum current equal to maximum flame size?
   A: No. NASA presents a case where a current peak corresponded to a compact microgravity flame, but this is not a general law. (RAG chunk QA-012, PSI-22)
17. Q: What is PSI-23 about?
   A: s-Flame studies time-dependent spherical diffusion flames, soot and radiative/flow-related extinction mechanisms. (RAG chunk QA-013, PSI-23)
18. Q: Which fuels are used in s-Flame?
   A: NASA discusses hydrogen/methane mixtures in soot-free cases and ethylene in sooty cases; specific run fuels require the original records. (RAG chunk QA-014, PSI-23)
19. Q: How do radiative and kinetic extinction differ?
   A: Radiative extinction emphasizes heat loss; kinetic or flow-related extinction emphasizes inability to sustain reaction under transport and flow conditions. Mechanism requires evidence. (RAG chunk QA-015, PSI-23)
20. Q: Does helium behave the same as nitrogen in s-Flame?
   A: No. NASA reports shifted extinction limits when helium is used instead of nitrogen for dilution. (RAG chunk QA-016, PSI-23)
